chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever performs an evil deed is respited regarding it for seven hours of the day. So if he says, 'I seek Forgiveness of Allah, the One there is no god except Him, the Living, the Eternal, and I repent to Him,' three times, it will not be written against him.

key_terms.لَمْ تُكْتَبْ عَلَيْهِ: It was not written against him

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication and time frame for a sin to be forgiven immediately after it is committed?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the divine mercy of a seven-hour 'grace period' granted after a sin, during which sincere repentance can erase the record of the transgression. The specific dhikr invokes Allah as 'Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum' (The Ever-Living, The Self-Subsisting), emphasizing reliance on His eternal power for forgiveness. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on immediate, heartfelt tawbah as a means to preserve one's spiritual ledger from being burdened by minor or major sins.
